land.text: French Togoland, the eastern part of Togoland divided between French and British zones; a French mandate from 20 July 1922, a UN trust territory 1946-1960, an autonomous republic within the French Union from 1955-1956

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic shape for 1958-1959 still holds the territory (267 of the 276 cells of modern Togo); the 1960 French shape holds 4. British Togoland, the western part, joined the Gold Coast (Ghana) in 1957 and is not Togo's land.

capitals.name: Lomé
capitals.note: Togo page infobox 'Capital and largest city: Lomé'; French Togoland page infobox 'Capital: Lomé'. Coordinates are Natural Earth's.

keyframe_review.note: 56,508 km2 for 1960-2023 against the page's 'Togo has an area equal to 56,785 km2' (ratio 0.995). The shape follows the modern frontier with Ghana, Burkina Faso and Benin; no page opened records a boundary change after the 27 April 1960 independence, and the only territorial transfer on the pages (British Togoland to the Gold Coast in 1957) lies outside this state.
Same outline as the 1960-2023 shape (56,508 km2); nothing on the page changes in 2024.

region.text: French Togoland: the eastern strip between Ghana and Benin from the coast to the Burkina Faso border

ledger.note: 27 April 1960: the Togolese Republic is proclaimed at Lomé. 'The Togolese Republic was proclaimed on 27 April 1960'; infobox 'Independence from France: 27 April 1960'. Second page (French Togoland): 'On 27 April 1960, in a smooth transition, Togo severed its constitutional ties with France'; the territory had been a UN trust territory since 1946 and an autonomous republic since the statute of 1955 and the referendum of 1956.

certainty.note: The frontier with Ghana follows the partition of Togoland into British and French zones (Togo page: collapse of the condominium on 7 December 1916; French Togoland infobox: 'Togoland partitioned: 27 December 1916'); neither page opened gives the origin of the Benin and Burkina Faso frontiers or records a dispute or a change after independence.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 (Togo, French Togoland). Togo has one Cliopatria row (1960-2024) and no territorial event after 27 April 1960 on either page. The pre-independence autonomy (autonomous republic within the French Union by the 1955 statute, constitution approved in the 1956 referendum, election won by Sylvanus Olympio in 1958) is a client relation of France that belongs in the French dossier; this dossier starts at the proclamation of the Togolese Republic. The French Togoland page is itself uneven on the autonomy (the text says 'By statute in 1955', the infobox 'Autonomy: 1956'), and the Togo page says British Togoland residents 'voted to join the Gold Coast ... in 1957' without a plebiscite date; the Ghana dossier owns that transfer. British Togoland (the western part, now the Volta Region) is not in Cliopatria's Togo shape.
